 Central Notes: Mitchell, Harden, Cunningham, Zubac
 By Arthur Hill |
 at November 13, 2026 10:00 am 
 The Cavaliers ’ inconsistent start to the season hasn’t shaken Donovan Mitchell ’s faith that the team is talented enough to compete for a title, writes Jamal Collier of ESPN . Cleveland is off to a 6-6 start, and the up-and-down nature of the team’s play was reflected this week with a double-digit loss at Charlotte on Monday, followed by a victory over the defending champions on Wednesday at Madison Square Garden.
 Questions persist about what the Cavs’ ceiling can be with a starting lineup featuring two ball-dominant guards in Mitchell and James Harden and two defensive-minded big men in Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen . The Cavaliers have a history of playoff disappointment since Mitchell arrived in 2022, and even though they reached the conference finals last season, they barely put up a fight while being swept by New York.
 “There’s a lot of belief in this group,” Mitchell said. “And the way that we have been able to battle through some adversity and continue to get better and better.” 
 Mitchell made a huge commitment to the organization this summer, Collier adds, accepting a four-year, $273MM extension when he could have potentially earned another $80MM by waiting one more year. Mitchell has repeatedly expressed his desire to stay in Cleveland, and he didn’t want contract speculation to be a distraction this season.
 “When doubt lingers in an organization, it’s not great,” coach Kenny Atkinson said. “Everybody’s just unsettled. So, the fact that Don locked it up, that was huge. It’s like a sigh of relief. You know you’re going to have your leader and it’s going to give you stability. It helps you just move forward quicker.” 
 There’s more from the Central Division:
 Harden made a statement with 32 points in the win at New York, his highest scoring total of the season, per Joe Vardon of The Athletic . Harden indicated that he’s still making adjustments after coming to the Cavaliers in a February trade. “I’m still trying to figure it out,” he said. “I think it’s my 18th year, so my name is James Harden. I used to score a lot of points. Now I still score points, but I’m finding other ways to impact the game as well. And I think that’s what people probably don’t understand.” 
 Pistons guard Cade Cunningham had a historic night with 52 points, 11 assists and no turnovers in Thursday’s double-overtime win at Washington. According to ESPN , Cunningham is the first player since at least 1978 to reach 50 points and 10 assists in a game without turning the ball over. “It was the best I’ve ever done it in my NBA career for sure,” he said.
 Pacers center Ivica Zubac has been working to add a reliable three-point shot to his arsenal, but he’s not ready to unveil it during games yet, states Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star . “I don’t want to put a timeline on it,” Zubac said. “I don’t know when it’s going to happen, but we work on it pretty much every day. I’m feeling a little more comfortable and comfortable, but still not quite comfortable enough to take them in a game. I think reps and working on it every day is going to help. My confidence is better.”
